### Summary

In a directive expression (`v-if`), a call whose argument is an object literal is reported as resolving to `any` / `unknown`, though the function returns `boolean`. The same call in an interpolation is not reported, nor is a call with a number argument.

### Version

- `vize` 0.443.0 (npm, bundled `@typescript/typescript-darwin-arm64` 7.0.2)
- Node v26.10.0, macOS arm64

`vize check` reports no type errors for the same file.

### Reproduction

`vize.config.json`

```json
{
  "linter": {
    "preset": "opinionated",
    "typeAware": true
  }
}
```

`tsconfig.json`

```json
{
  "compilerOptions": {
    "target": "ESNext",
    "module": "ESNext",
    "moduleResolution": "bundler",
    "strict": true,
    "skipLibCheck": true,
    "lib": ["ESNext", "DOM"]
  },
  "include": ["*.vue", "*.ts"]
}
```

`DirectiveObjectArg.vue`

```vue
<script setup lang="ts">
const isA = (o: { kind: string }): boolean => o.kind === "a";
const isPositive = (n: number): boolean => n > 0;
</script>

<template>
  <p v-if="isA({ kind: 'a' })">reported</p>
  <p v-if="isPositive(1)">not reported</p>
  <p>{{ isA({ kind: "a" }) }}</p>
</template>
```

`vize lint --format plain DirectiveObjectArg.vue`

```
  DirectiveObjectArg.vue:7:12 warning type/no-unsafe-template-binding Template directive expression resolves to an unsafe `any` or `unknown` type
```
